sections.html:
Stillwater is a college city in north-central Oklahoma, about 60 miles north-northeast of downtown Oklahoma City and 63 miles west of downtown Tulsa by road. Oklahoma State University reports 30,683 students enrolled for Fall 2026, made up of 22,895 undergraduates, 6,694 graduate students, 1,082 professional students and 12 non-credit students. That large student and employee population sits behind local housing demand, so a student-oriented rental is a different kind of asset from a family home.

If you own from out of town, as a parent or an heir, a house with tenants or deferred repairs can be easier to sell as-is than to renovate from a distance. Payne County values and bills Stillwater properties.

Stillwater requires a license for any short-term rental, under Ordinance No. 3604.

RuleDetail
LicenseAnnual license required to manage or operate a short-term rental
Density capNo more than 20 percent of a residential block
ApplicationProof of ownership and state tax compliance
TransferLicenses are non-transferable
Fees$100 initial, $10 renewal

The non-transferable license matters if you bought a house with a license in place, or are selling one. A new owner cannot take it over. A buyer who plans to run the house as a rental has to apply on their own and must fit under the block's density cap. The city publishes a list of active licenses, which is a quick way to see whether your block is crowded, and Development Services at 405-742-8220 answers questions. If the house was an unlicensed short-term rental, talk to a local attorney before you list.

Code Enforcement is a division of the police department, and it issues citations for structural and non-structural problems. Dilapidated or unsecured structures can be reported with an online complaint form. The city's nuisance list covers:

  • Grass, weeds or brush over 12 inches that create a health, safety or welfare problem
  • Broken windows, roof and gutter problems, missing siding and peeling paint
  • Inoperable or untagged vehicles and trailers
  • Dilapidated, open or vacant buildings, which may not stay boarded for more than 36 months
  • Trash carts with lids that do not close

If a problem stays unfixed, the city may hire a contractor to mow, board up, demolish or clear debris, bill the owner, and place a tax lien on the property to recover the cost. Judicial remedies can include fines of up to $549 per day per violation, depending on the violation. Each violation has its own time limit.

An open nuisance case is a loose end for a seller. Resolve it or disclose it, because a lien tied to the property can surface during title work.

Stillwater sits in Tornado Alley, with frequent spring tornado watches and warnings. Summer highs reach or pass 100 degrees about ten times a year, and winters bring snow, so heating and cooling systems, attic insulation and roof condition all come up in an inspection.

The Payne County Assessor offers an exemption for up to 100 square feet of an eligible tornado shelter or safe room added after January 1, 2002. If your house has one, keep the installation record and the exemption paperwork for the buyer.

Stillwater Public Schools covers almost all of the city, including every residential area. A small piece of the city occupied by airport property is in Morrison Public Schools. The Stillwater Utilities Authority provides electric, water, wastewater and solid waste service, so ask the city how it handles a final reading and account transfer at closing.

The Payne County Assessor is at 315 W. 6th Avenue, Suite 102, Stillwater, phone 405-747-8300. Relief programs include:

  • Homestead exemption: reduces the assessed value of an eligible primary residence by $1,000, generally if you own and occupy the home on January 1.
  • Additional homestead: another $1,000 for qualifying homeowners with household income of $30,000 or less.
  • Senior valuation limitation: caps increases in fair cash value for a head of household age 65 or older who meets the income limit, without freezing the bill.
  • Exemptions for disabled veteran owners and surviving spouses, plus the storm shelter exemption.

To dispute a value, a taxpayer has 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written complaint with the assessor. Payne County also runs an online appeal system. Call 405-747-8300 to confirm your dates.

A listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash sale all work in Stillwater. Which fits depends on the house and how soon you need to be done. A listing suits a house in good condition near campus when you can wait on showings and a buyer's loan. A cash sale suits a house with tenant wear, deferred repairs, a code notice, or an owner who lives far away.

Before choosing, collect your deed, lease copies if any, utility account details and your latest tax statement. If the house was a short-term rental, add the license record.

faqs.a: Payne County. The Payne County Assessor in Stillwater handles valuation and exemptions, and the county treasurer bills the tax.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Stillwater short-term rental license?
faqs.a: No. Ordinance No. 3604 makes licenses non-transferable, so the new owner has to apply and must fit under the 20 percent block density cap.

faqs.q: How big is Oklahoma State University?
faqs.a: The university reports 30,683 students enrolled for Fall 2026, including 22,895 undergraduates and 6,694 graduate students.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a Stillwater code notice before selling?
faqs.a: The city may hire a contractor, bill you and place a tax lien on the property, and fines of up to $549 per day per violation are possible for some violations. Clear the case or disclose it before closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest a Payne County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written complaint with the county assessor. Call 405-747-8300 to confirm your dates.
